```{r}
#loading packages and palmerpenguins to use as for a dataset 
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
```

```{r}

#using copilot to generate a ggplt scatter plot using penguins dataset
#plot bill_length_mm on the x-axis and bill_depth_mm on the y-axis
#colour points by species and use geom_point with size 3
#add minimal theme and clean labels

plot <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Bill Length vs Bill Depth in Penguins",
       x = "Bill Length (mm)",
       y = "Bill Depth (mm)",
       color = "Species")

plot

```

```{r}
#generate a boxplot comparing flipper_length_mm across different species, faceted by island, using custom colour palettes 

plot2 <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ island) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Adelie" = "#1f77b4", "Chinstrap" = "#ff7f0e", "Gentoo" = "#2ca02c")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Flipper Length by Species and Island",
       x = "Species",
       y = "Flipper Length (mm)",
       fill = "Species")

plot2
```

```{r}
penguins
#generate a smooth line plot of the penguins data set 
#x-axis is body mass and y-axis is bill length, colour lines by species 
#include the range of standard error 
#add theme classic and clean labels 

plot3 <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Bill Length vs Body Mass in Penguins",
       x = "Body Mass (g)",
       y = "Bill Length (mm)",
       color = "Species")
plot3

```

```{r}
#Show me how to load the built-in iris dataset and use ggplot2 to build a scatter plot of Sepal.Length versus Sepal.Width colored by Species
plot5 <- ggplot(data = iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Sepal Length vs Sepal Width in Iris Dataset",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)",
       y = "Sepal Width (cm)",
       color = "Species")
plot5
